title: Systemic Policy Failure — Institutionalized Evasion of Legal Accountability

incident.date: 5 de julho de 2024 — Voo LA8159 — Aeroporto SCL (ver Fatos Fixos do Incidente)

incident_timestamp_display: 5 de julho de 2024 — Voo LA8159 — Aeroporto SCL (ver Fatos Fixos do Incidente)
allegation_summary: It is alleged that the LA8159 incident exposed a systemic, institutionalized policy failure at LATAM Airlines whereby (1) staff operate under a 'no documentation at the airport' policy for passenger removals, (2) staff describe the passenger as 'disruptivo' (disruptive) which serves as a corporate classification that automatically forecloses all procedural remedies, (3) the Sales department (Ventas) is used as an off-book document fabrication channel, (4) templates designed for flight contingencies are repurposed for passenger removals avoiding statutory denied boarding obligations, and (5) the company maintains a 'no solution' policy for all cases classified as 'disruptive passenger.' This institutional architecture creates a de facto immunity zone where passenger rights under CACH, LPDC, and the Montreal Convention are systematically negated through procedural design rather than isolated staff error.

articles.article_name: Codigo Aeronautico de Chile, Art. 133 — Denegacion de Embarque
articles.article_text:
1. A eleccion del pasajero:

a) Embarcar en el siguiente vuelo que tenga disponible el transportador, o en un transporte alternativo, si es que decidiera persistir en el contrato de transporte aereo.  
b) El reembolso del monto total pagado por el billete, si el pasajero se desiste del contrato de transporte aereo y este no hubiera comenzado su ejecucion.
articles.applicability_rationale: CACH Art. 133 establishes mandatory procedures that carriers must follow upon denied boarding. The existence of an institutional policy that systematically circumvents these procedures — through refusal to document, classification of passengers as 'disruptive' to foreclose remedies, use of off-book document production channels, and repurposing of inapplicable templates — constitutes a structural violation of Art. 133 that goes beyond individual staff misconduct to an organizational design failure. The 'no solution for disruptive passengers' statement by the Duty Supervisor reveals that this is not an isolated incident but an institutional position. | legacy paraphrase: El transportador podra denegar el embarque a uno o mas pasajeros contra su voluntad, para lo cual debera: 1.- A eleccion del pasajero... 2.- El transportador debera ofrecer una compensacion al pasajero afectado...

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Codigo Aeronautico de Chile, Art. 131 — Obligaciones del transportador respecto del pasajero
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CACH.Art.131 from bcn.cl/leychile to confirm scope of carrier obligations
Verify whether Art. 131 imposes documentary obligations on the carrier when denying boarding or removing a passenger
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 131 likely establishes general carrier obligations toward passengers that frame the duty to provide proper documentation and transparent procedures. The institutional policy of issuing unsigned documents and instructing staff to 'adjust reality' may constitute a systemic breach of these general obligations.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Identified as the general-obligations article that contextualizes Art. 133's specific denied-boarding rules.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Codigo Aeronautico de Chile, Art. 134 — Compensaciones por denegacion de embarque
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CACH.Art.134 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether Art. 134 specifies compensation amounts and whether the carrier's reframing of removal as 'voluntary' would defeat the passenger's right to compensation under this article
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: If the carrier systematically recharacterizes involuntary removals as voluntary disembarkations, this would defeat the compensation regime of Art. 134, making the institutional policy a mechanism to evade statutory compensation duties.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Companion to Art. 133 in the denied-boarding compensation framework.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Codigo Aeronautico de Chile, Art. 135 — Informacion al pasajero
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CACH.Art.135 from bcn.cl/leychile
Verify whether this article mandates that the carrier inform the passenger in writing of their rights upon denied boarding
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: The admission that 'none of our documents have a signature' and the use of inapplicable templates suggests systematic non-compliance with passenger information duties that Art. 135 may impose.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Hypothesized as the information-duty provision within the CACH denied-boarding framework.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Ley de Proteccion al Consumidor (19.496), Art. 3 — Derechos basicos del consumidor
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.LPC.Art.3 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm that letra b) (derecho a informacion veraz y oportuna) and letra e) (derecho a reparacion e indemnizacion) apply to air transport consumers
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: The institutional policy of producing unsigned documents, instructing staff to 'adjust reality,' and reframing involuntary removal as voluntary likely violates the consumer's basic right to truthful and timely information (Art. 3 letra b) and the right to adequate reparation (Art. 3 letra e).
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. LPC applies subsidiarily to air transport where CACH does not provide specific consumer protections.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Ley de Proteccion al Consumidor (19.496), Art. 12 — Obligacion de cumplir lo ofrecido y pactado
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.LPC.Art.12 from bcn.cl/leychile
Verify applicability to air transport contracts and whether systematic evasion of contractual obligations through institutional policy constitutes a violation
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: A systemic policy designed to avoid honoring the transport contract (by recharacterizing denial of service as passenger-initiated) would violate the obligation to comply with what was offered and agreed upon.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. General contractual compliance obligation under consumer law.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Ley de Proteccion al Consumidor (19.496), Art. 23 — Infraccion por negativa injustificada de venta o prestacion de servicio
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.LPC.Art.23 from bcn.cl/leychile
Determine whether unjustified refusal to provide contracted air transport service, combined with institutional mechanisms to avoid accountability, triggers this provision
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: The systematic denial of service combined with institutional mechanisms to evade documentation and accountability may constitute an unjustified refusal to provide contracted services under Art. 23.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Addresses unjustified service refusal which is the practical effect of the institutional evasion policy.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Ley de Proteccion al Consumidor (19.496), Art. 28 — Publicidad engañosa e induccion a error
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.LPC.Art.28 from bcn.cl/leychile
Assess whether the instruction to 'adjust reality' in official documents constitutes inducing error in the consumer regarding the nature of the service denial
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: The instruction to 'adjust reality' in documentation provided to the passenger could constitute inducing error regarding the true nature and cause of the service denial, potentially engaging Art. 28's prohibition on misleading communications.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. The 'adjusting reality' instruction suggests deliberate misrepresentation in carrier-to-consumer communications.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Codigo Civil, Art. 1545 — Fuerza obligatoria del contrato (pacta sunt servanda)
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CC.Art.1545 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm applicability to air transport contracts and whether institutional policy to evade contractual performance constitutes a violation of the binding force of contracts
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: The systematic institutional design to avoid honoring the transport contract — through recharacterization, unsigned documents, and reality-adjustment instructions — violates the fundamental principle that a validly formed contract is law for the parties.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Foundational civil law principle underlying all contractual claims.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Codigo Civil, Art. 1546 — Buena fe contractual
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CC.Art.1546 from bcn.cl/leychile
Verify whether an institutional policy designed to evade accountability through document manipulation and factual recharacterization constitutes bad faith in contractual performance
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: An institutionalized policy of producing unsigned documents, instructing staff to adjust factual records, and reframing involuntary removal as voluntary represents a paradigmatic case of bad faith in contractual execution, violating Art. 1546's requirement that contracts be performed in good faith.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Core good-faith obligation that the institutional evasion policy directly contradicts.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Codigo Civil, Art. 1556 — Indemnizacion de perjuicios (daño emergente y lucro cesante)
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CC.Art.1556 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm scope of compensable damages when contractual breach is accompanied by institutional bad faith
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: The systemic nature of the evasion policy aggravates the damages flowing from the contractual breach, potentially expanding the scope of compensable harm under Art. 1556 to include consequential losses caused by the deliberate obstruction of remedies.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Damages provision relevant to quantifying harm from institutional evasion.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Codigo Civil, Art. 2314 — Responsabilidad extracontractual por hecho ilicito
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CC.Art.2314 from bcn.cl/leychile
Assess whether the institutional policy of document manipulation and factual distortion constitutes an independent tortious act beyond mere contractual breach
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: The deliberate institutional design to evade legal accountability — through unsigned documents, reality-adjustment instructions, and systematic recharacterization — may constitute an independent tortious act (hecho ilicito) causing harm beyond the original contractual breach, engaging extracontractual liability.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Relevant where institutional conduct transcends contractual breach into independent wrongdoing.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Codigo Aeronautico de Chile, Art. 150 — Responsabilidad del transportador por incumplimiento
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CACH.Art.150 from bcn.cl/leychile
Verify whether this article establishes carrier liability for failure to perform the transport contract and whether institutional evasion mechanisms aggravate liability
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 150 likely establishes the carrier's liability framework for failure to perform the transport contract. The existence of an institutional policy designed to circumvent this liability framework would itself constitute an aggravating factor.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Specific CACH liability provision that the evasion policy is designed to circumvent.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Ley de Proteccion al Consumidor (19.496), Art. 16 — Clausulas abusivas
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.LPC.Art.16 from bcn.cl/leychile
Determine whether internal policies that systematically deny consumer remedies through procedural manipulation constitute abusive clauses or practices under Art. 16
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: If the carrier's conditions of carriage or internal policies effectively strip passengers of their legal remedies through procedural manipulation (unsigned documents, reality adjustment), these may constitute abusive contractual practices under Art. 16.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Addresses whether institutional evasion mechanisms function as de facto abusive clauses.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Ley 19.628 sobre Proteccion de la Vida Privada, Art. 2 — Definiciones y principio de calidad de datos
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.LPDP.Art.2 from bcn.cl/leychile

candidate_articles.preliminary_view: The instruction to 'adjust reality' in documentation may implicate data protection law if it involves falsifying passenger records in the carrier's systems, violating the principle that personal data must be accurate and truthful.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Relevant if 'adjusting reality' involves manipulation of personal data records.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Ley 19.628 sobre Proteccion de la Vida Privada, Art. 9 — Derecho a modificacion de datos inexactos
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.LPDP.Art.9 from bcn.cl/leychile

candidate_articles.preliminary_view: If the carrier creates false records characterizing the passenger as disruptive or as having voluntarily disembarked, the passenger has a right under Art. 9 to demand modification of these inexact data, and the institutional policy of creating such records constitutes a systematic violation.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Addresses the data-correction dimension of the institutional falsification policy.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Constitucion Politica de la Republica, Art. 19 N°3 — Igual proteccion de la ley en el ejercicio de derechos
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CPR.Art.19 numeral 3 from bcn.cl/leychile

Assess whether an institutional policy designed to prevent passengers from exercising legal remedies constitutes a violation of the constitutional guarantee of equal protection in the exercise of rights, considering horizontal application (eficacia horizontal) of constitutional rights
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: The institutional design to prevent passengers from obtaining proper documentation and exercising their legal rights may engage the constitutional guarantee of equal protection in the exercise of rights, particularly through the doctrine of horizontal application of fundamental rights (Drittwirkung). However, direct constitutional claims against private parties require careful doctrinal analysis.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Constitutional dimension of the systematic obstruction of legal remedies.

open_questions.question: ¿Declaró el pasajero haber recibido o rechazado alguna oferta de compensación?
¿Existen registros internos de LATAM sobre gestión de compensación?
¿Se han obtenido mediante requerimiento formal los registros internos del vuelo?
¿Existen manuales, correos o directrices corporativas que instruyan el manejo documental de incidentes?
¿Consta en el expediente el PNR o boarding pass del pasajero?
¿Existe grabación de la respuesta del pasajero a la pregunta de [[SPK-diego-latam-supervisor]]?
¿Existen otros incidentes documentados con el mismo patrón?
¿Logró el pasajero tomar vuelo alternativo, en qué condiciones?
¿Existe grabación (audio, video o CCTV del aeropuerto) del momento exacto de la remoción del pasajero del vuelo que confirme que fue involuntaria?

¿Existe comunicación escrita posterior (correo electrónico, carta, mensaje en plataforma de reclamos, o registro en sistema CRM de LATAM) donde se hayan ofrecido al pasajero las opciones del Art. 133 N° 1 (embarque alternativo o reembolso)?
¿Se ofreció compensación al pasajero en algún momento posterior al incidente, ya sea en el aeropuerto, por vía telefónica, escrita o a través del sistema de reclamos de LATAM o del SERNAC?

¿Existen manuales internos, directrices operacionales, protocolos de handling o instrucciones escritas de LATAM que formalicen las prácticas de no firmar documentos, reencuadrar remociones como voluntarias, o 'ajustar la realidad' en los registros?

¿La normativa reglamentaria de la JAC o la DGAC establece requisitos formales de documentación (formularios, firmas, constancias) para las denegaciones de embarque bajo el Art. 133 del Código Aeronáutico?
¿Cuál fue el destino final del pasajero tras la remoción, en qué vuelo o medio de transporte llegó, y cuál fue el retraso efectivo total sufrido?
¿Existen testigos (otros pasajeros, tripulantes, personal de tierra, policía aeroportuaria) que presenciaron la orden directa de desembarque y pueden declarar sobre su carácter involuntario?
¿Se presentó reclamo formal ante la DGAC o la JAC por esta denegación de embarque, y existe resolución o informe de fiscalización al respecto?

¿Existen copias de los documentos sin firma que LATAM generó respecto de este incidente (informes internos, formularios de denegación, reportes de irregularidad) que permitan verificar su contenido y contrastar con los hechos grabados?
